item.title: Woman arrested for allegedly shoplifting from Columbus Walmart - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COLUMBUS – A woman was arrested Sunday after a reported shoplifting incident at Walmart in Columbus, according to the Columbus Police Department.

Police said officers responded March 29 to the store after receiving a report of shoplifting.

When officers arrived, they made contact with the suspect, identified as Kelisha Blevins. Following an investigation, Blevins was taken into custody without incident, police said.

Blevins was initially charged with shoplifting. During the arrest, officers also learned she had outstanding warrants with the Columbus Police Department, according to police.

As a result, she was additionally charged with felony shoplifting.

The Columbus Police Department said it remains committed to protecting local businesses and holding offenders accountable.

item.title: Vancleave man arrested on sexual battery, molestation charges - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BILOXI — A Vancleave man has been arrested on felony charges of sexual battery and molestation following an investigation involving a minor, authorities said.

The Biloxi Police Department assisted the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office on March 30, 2026, in arresting Mitchell Linn Dye, 39, on two active felony warrants.

The charges stem from an ongoing investigation in which a 15-year-old reported she was sexually assaulted by Dye in February 2026, according to officials.

Dye made an initial court appearance before Judge Mark Watts, who set bail at $100,000 for each charge, for a total of $200,000.

Authorities have not released additional details about the investigation.

item.title: Tyree Jones marks final day as Jackson police chief, thanks city and department leaders - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Hinds County Sheriff Tyree Jones said Tuesday was his final day serving as chief of the Jackson Police Department, bringing to a close a seven-month stretch in which he held both leadership roles.

In a statement, Jones said,

“Today is my final day serving as Chief of Police for the Jackson Police Department.” He added, “Leading this department during a critical transition period has been an honor, and I am grateful to Mayor John Horhn for his trust, confidence, and support over the past seven months.”

Jones said the experience was especially meaningful in the context of his long law enforcement career.

“Serving in the dual role of Hinds County Sheriff and Chief of Police has been one of the greatest highlights of my 26-year career, and I remain forever thankful for the opportunity,” he said.

He also thanked his family for their support during his time in the role.

“I want to thank my family for their unwavering support throughout this journey,” Jones said. “Their strength and encouragement have allowed me to serve our community with focus and commitment.”

Jones also praised officers and staff with both the Jackson Police Department and the Hinds County Sheriff’s Office.

“I am also deeply grateful to the men and women of both JPD and HCSO for their professionalism, dedication, and support in ensuring stability and continuity of operations in both departments,” he said. “Their service to our community is invaluable, and I am proud to stand with them.”

Jones said he remains optimistic about the city’s future and plans to continue working with Jackson leaders and public safety partners as sheriff.

“As a lifelong Jacksonian, I admire the progress our city continues to make, and it has been an honor to contribute to that progress,” he said. “In my ongoing role as Sheriff, I look forward to continuing strong partnerships with the City of Jackson, our community, and all public safety stakeholders.”

He also said he intends to support incoming Jackson Police Chief Dr. Rashell Brackney during the transition.

“I also look forward to supporting incoming Chief Dr. Rashell Brackney throughout this transition and as she assumes leadership of the department,” Jones said.

Jones closed his statement by thanking the city directly.

“Thank you, Jackson, for your support and for the privilege to serve,” he said. “Jackson Rising.”

item.title: Two charged after robbery and assault reported at Starkville Sprint Mart - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
STARKVILLE – Two people were arrested Monday after a reported robbery and assault at a Starkville convenience store, according to the Starkville Police Department.

Officers were called at 9:55 a.m. to Sprint Mart, 12258 Highway 182 East, for a report of an assault and robbery.

When officers arrived, they spoke with those involved. Police said the victim reported being physically assaulted during the incident and was evaluated at the scene.

After an investigation, authorities charged Terrell Prater, 25, of Starkville, with robbery. Diona McNeal, 41, of Houston, was charged as an accessory to robbery.

No weapons were involved, according to the department. Both suspects were taken to the Oktibbeha County Jail.

The case remains under investigation. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Starkville Police Department at 662-323-4131, Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers at 800-530-7151, or submit an anonymous tip through the department’s website. Crime Stoppers may offer a cash reward.

item.title: Tupelo man arrested on fentanyl charges after Lee County search warrant - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LEE COUNTY – A Tupelo man was arrested on fentanyl-related charges after a search warrant was carried out in southern Lee County, according to the Lee County Sheriff’s Office.

Sheriff Jim Johnson said the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, working with the Tupelo Police Department and the North Mississippi Narcotics Unit, executed the search warrant March 24.

Investigators arrested Andre Deshone Green, 48, of Tupelo.

Green was charged with possession of a Schedule II controlled substance, identified as fentanyl. He also was taken into custody on two circuit court capias warrants tied to the sale of fentanyl, according to the sheriff’s office.

A justice court judge set Green’s bond at $5,000 on the possession charge. He remains jailed without bond on the two capias warrants.

The sheriff’s office said additional charges could be presented later to a grand jury.

item.title: Teen driver, school bus involved in Jones County crash; 2 taken to hospital - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – A teenage driver and a Jones County School District bus were involved in a two-vehicle crash Monday morning in the Powers community, according to the Jones County Sheriff’s Department.

The crash happened on Highway 184 at the intersection of Lawn Haven Church Road. Authorities said the bus and a Toyota passenger car driven by a teenage girl collided there.

The driver of the Toyota declined medical transport.

The school bus driver and one of the seven students on the bus were transported by EMServ Ambulance Service to South Central Regional Medical Center for treatment.

Several agencies responded to the scene, including the Mississippi Highway Patrol, Jones County Sheriff’s Department, EMServ Ambulance Service, Powers Fire & Rescue, M&M Fire & Rescue, Sandersville Fire & Rescue and the Jones County School District.

Highway 184 was closed at the crash site while crews responded and investigators worked the scene.

item.title: Pearl police resolve domestic disturbance at motel after armed standoff - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL – Pearl police said an armed domestic disturbance at a motel Monday afternoon ended peacefully after a brief standoff and negotiations.

According to the Pearl Police Department, officers were called around 2:30 p.m. March 30 to the Super 8 Motel at 111 Airport Road after a woman reported that an ex was attempting to steal her vehicle.

Officers with the Patrol and Special Operations divisions responded and began an investigation. Police said officers found that the woman had injuries consistent with domestic violence.

Authorities learned which motel room the man was staying in and tried to make contact, but he refused to answer the door, police said. Officers were able to reach him by phone, and he told them he was not coming out.

Because of the domestic violence nature of the call, the situation was treated as an armed subject incident and turned over to the Pearl Police Department’s Special Weapons and Tactics Team, according to police.

An officer certified in hostage negotiations spoke with the man for about 30 minutes, police said, leading to the man exiting the room and surrendering without incident.

Police said the case ended peacefully and thanked the officers involved in bringing the situation to a resolution.

item.title: MDWFP Chief of Law Enforcement Recognized as Patriotic Employer - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks (MDWFP) is pleased to announce Jerry Carter, MDWFP Chief of Law Enforcement has been recognized as a Patriotic Employer by the Employer Support of the Guard and Reserve (ESGR), a Department of Defense Office.

The ESGR Patriotic Employer Award is given to supervisors and leaders who demonstrate strong support for Guard and Reserve members through flexible policies, understanding of military responsibilities, and a commitment to maintaining open communication.

Carter was nominated for the award by Sergeant Major Larry Primeaux of the Army National Guard, who also serves with MDWFP’s Law Enforcement K-9 Unit. This award was in recognition of Carter’s outstanding support of Primeaux who serves in the United States Armed Forces Guard and Reserve. The Patriotic Employer Award reflects the high level of commitment shown to accommodating military obligations, promoting a supportive work environment, and recognizing the value of service to the nation.

Nearly one-third of the United States Armed Forces is comprised of the Guard and Reserve, making employer support essential to maintaining military readiness. Carter’s recognition highlights the important role MDWFP leadership plays in supporting employees who serve both their communities and their country.

“Our partnership with the National Guard is built on a shared commitment to service,” said Jerry Carter, MDWFP Chief of Law Enforcement. “We’re proud to support those who serve both in our counties and country, and we value the strength and leadership they bring to our agency.”

Officials said tips leading to an arrest could result in a reward of up to $2,500, and callers may remain anonymous.

item.title: Jackson Mayor Urges Residents to Apply for Tornado Recovery Program Before Deadline - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Mayor John Horhn is urging eligible homeowners to apply for a state-administered recovery program before a fast-approaching deadline to receive assistance for storm-damaged homes.

The Mississippi Homeowner Rehabilitation & Reconstruction Program, administered by the Mississippi Development Authority, provides federally funded aid to low- and moderate-income homeowners whose homes were damaged or destroyed during the April 8-11, 2024, tornadoes and straight-line winds.

Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. Sunday, April 5, 2026.

“Many Jackson families are still working to recover from these devastating storms, and this program can provide critical help to rebuild what was lost,” Horhn said in a statement. “I encourage every eligible homeowner to apply before the deadline and take advantage of this opportunity for support.”

According to the Mississippi Housing Recovery program, applicants must have unrepaired storm damage, own and occupy the home as their primary residence and meet income requirements at or below 80% of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s area median income. Eligible properties include those located in Hinds County.

Homeowners can apply online, by phone or in person through the Mississippi Housing Recovery website. Applicants should be prepared to provide documentation including proof of identity, income, homeownership, residency, insurance coverage and any disaster assistance previously received.

For Jackson-area residents seeking in-person help, an intake center is available at the Edwards Community Center in Edwards. There is no cost to apply or participate in the program.

More information is available at mshousingrecovery.com or by calling 866-981-7727.

item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
HARRISON COUNTY — Authorities are asking for the public’s help in locating a missing 43-year-old man who has not been heard from since early March.

Sheriff Matt Haley said Kelvin Mark Fuqua last spoke with family members on March 3, 2026, and has not returned home or contacted relatives or close friends since that time.

Fuqua is a Black male, 5 feet 6 inches tall and weighing about 195 pounds. He is partially bald with some brown hair, has a beard and brown eyes. Officials said he also has multiple tattoos on his face and a nose piercing.

Investigators said Fuqua did not leave his home with a vehicle or a phone, and it is unknown what he was wearing when he was last seen.

Anyone with information about Fuqua’s whereabouts is urged to contact the Harrison County Sheriff’s Office at 228-897-1364 or Mississippi Coast Crime Stoppers at 877-787-5898.

item.title: Federal grand jury indicts 8 in North Mississippi drug case; arrests made - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
OXFORD — A federal grand jury has indicted eight individuals on drug distribution charges following a months-long, multi-agency investigation in north Mississippi, authorities said.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary announced that the indictments were returned March 25, 2026, in the Northern District of Mississippi. All eight defendants were arrested Monday. One of the individuals also faces a charge of being a felon in possession of firearms.

According to court documents the following individuals were indicted by a federal grand jury in the Northern District of Mississippi: • Gary “Rooster” Ransom, 49, of Clarksdale, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution and felon in possession of firearms • Daniel Baker, 40, of Cleveland, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution • Madeline Tonos, 31, of Cleveland, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution • Patrick Smith, 34, of Cleveland, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution • Valerie Ingram, 42, of Cleveland, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution • Joshua Fulton, 40, of Cleveland, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution • Londyn Todd, 23, of Cleveland, Mississippi, indicted for drug distribution • Merrick Smith, 47, of Dallas, Texas, indicted for drug distribution

Leary said the case is tied to the Homeland Security Task Force, a partnership of federal and state law enforcement agencies focused on combating drug trafficking and related violent crime.

“This HSTF operation stemmed from a months-long multi-agency investigation,” Leary said, crediting cooperation between agencies, including the Cleveland Police Department and the FBI.

The FBI is leading the investigation, with assistance from the U.S. Marshals Service and Cleveland Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Chad Doleac and Sam Stringfellow are prosecuting the case.

Authorities emphasized that indictments are allegations and not proof of guilt. All defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Frank Garcia, Chickasaw County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CHICKASAW COUNTY — A Houston man who walked away from his home carrying his belongings in February 1994 has never been found, and investigators are still seeking information that could help solve his disappearance.

Frank Garcia, a 35-year-old Hispanic man, was last seen on Feb. 16, 1994, walking away from his residence on Highway 8 East in Houston. He was carrying two garbage bags of clothes, a 19-inch television and a box of important papers at the time.

Garcia was not reported missing until nearly a week later, when he failed to pick up two paychecks from his employer and no one had heard from him.

He is described as 5 feet, 5 inches tall, weighing approximately 140 pounds, with brown hair and brown eyes. Garcia has tattoos reading “Nancy” on one arm and “Ginger” on the other.

The case is being investigated by the Mississippi Department of Public Safety and the Chickasaw County Sheriff’s Department. Garcia remains missing as of the publication of this report.

Anyone with information on Garcia’s whereabouts is asked to contact the Mississippi Department of Public Safety at (662) 563-6400 or the Chickasaw County Sheriff’s Department at (662) 456-3513.

item.title: Lary Aaron to headline Legacy League Hot Stove event April 3 in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Lary Aaron, son of baseball legend Hank Aaron, will make a special guest appearance April 3 at a Hot Stove event in Jackson to support the inaugural season of the Legacy League, organizers announced.

The event, sponsored by Colombean Coffee, is set for 2 p.m. at the Mississippi Sports Hall of Fame. It is free and open to the public and will feature a one-hour interview session, question-and-answer segment and autograph opportunities with former professional players.

Aaron, who followed his father into baseball, played outfield at Florida A&M University before being selected by the Atlanta Braves in the 32nd round of the 1981 MLB Draft. He spent two seasons in the Braves’ minor league system before transitioning into a long career in scouting, including nearly two decades with the Milwaukee Brewers organization.

Organizers said Aaron has remained active in mentoring athletes and promoting the values associated with his father’s legacy, including integrity and dedication to the sport.

Other scheduled guests for the event include former Braves and Falcons standout Brian Jordan, World Series champion Marquis Grissom and former Braves pitcher Jair Jurrjens.

The appearance is part of a promotional push ahead of the launch of the Legacy League, a developmental baseball league designed to provide opportunities for collegiate players. The league’s ownership group includes former professional athletes such as Tracy McGrady, Andruw Jones, Jordan, Jurrjens, Grissom and Bernard Gilkey.

League play is scheduled to begin May 26, with a 28-game season to be held at Smith-Wills Stadium.

item.title: Five killed, one injured in train-van crash in Stone County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
STONE COUNTY – Five people were killed and a sixth was seriously injured Friday afternoon when a train collided with a van in Stone County, according to WLOX.

Stone County Sheriff Todd Stewart told WLOX the crash happened around 1 p.m. at Pump Branch Road, just off Highway 49. First responders had to cut their way through the woods to reach the wreckage, the station reported.

Authorities said six people were inside the van at the time of the crash. Stone County Coroner Wayne Flurry confirmed that five of them died at the scene, and the sixth person was airlifted to a hospital in New Orleans.

WLOX later reported the five people killed were identified as 26-year-old Ryan C. Peterson, 23-year-old Demarcus Perkins, 45-year-old Kristina Carver, and Carver’s two daughters, 22-year-old Emley Chamblee and 20-year-old Sarabeth Chamblee.

The station also reported that the railroad crossing at Pump Branch Road does not have crossing arms or lights. Stone County District 1 Supervisor Jimmy Springs told WLOX that crossarms are planned for the crossing, but installation could take up to a year.

item.title: Casino burglary suspect caught by Tunica County K-9 after lengthy chase - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – A Tunica man was arrested Friday night after authorities said he was linked to a vehicle burglary at a Robinsonville casino, then led deputies on a chase that ended in a crash and foot pursuit.

The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office said deputies were called around 9:14 p.m. Friday to a casino in Robinsonville after receiving a report of a vehicle burglary in the parking lot.

Witnesses provided a description of the suspects’ vehicle, and that information was broadcast to patrol deputies, according to the sheriff’s office.

At about 9:52 p.m., a deputy spotted a vehicle matching the description near Old Highway 61 and Casino Strip Drive and attempted a traffic stop. Authorities said the driver refused to stop, leading deputies on a high-speed chase before losing control of the vehicle and fleeing on foot.

Deputies then pursued the suspect on foot and used a sheriff’s office K-9 to make the arrest, officials said.

Authorities identified the suspect as Deonte Taylor, 20, of Tunica. Taylor suffered a dog bite during the apprehension and was treated at an area hospital before being taken to the Tunica County Jail.

Taylor was charged with failure to stop, possession of a stolen firearm, possession of burglary tools, conspiracy, burglary of a vehicle and felony fleeing.

The sheriff’s office said Taylor had also been out on bond in connection with a 2023 triple homicide case in Tunica County, where he faced capital murder and other charges.

Officials said Taylor was given a $45,000 bond on the new charges.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact CrimeStoppers at 662-910-0400 or the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411.

item.title: Opera Mississippi to Perform 'Songs for a New World' in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Opera Mississippi will bring Tony Award-winning composer Jason Robert Brown’s “Songs for a New World” to Duling Hall in Jackson on April 24-25, offering audiences two nights of professional musical theatre centered on themes of change, resilience and hope.

Tickets are $35 per person. Each evening begins with an Opera Happy Hour at 6 p.m., with the concert starting at 7 p.m. Duling Hall is located at 622 Duling Ave.

The production features four professional vocalists: John Christopher Adams, Maryann Kyle, Peter Lake and Sarah Stembel. They will be performing a song cycle that blends pop, gospel and contemporary musical theatre. Rather than a traditional narrative, the show presents a series of self-contained scenes depicting people at pivotal moments of transformation.

Brown, who won a Tony Award for “The Bridges of Madison County,” wrote “Songs for a New World” as his debut stage work. The piece has since become a staple of regional and professional musical theatre nationally.

Founded in 1945, Opera Mississippi is the ninth oldest continuously operating opera company in the United States and the state’s only professional opera company. The organization’s mission includes educational outreach, emerging artist development and preserving the operatic art form.

Tickets are available at operamississippi.org .

item.description:
JACKSON COUNTY — An 83-year-old Jackson County man is facing a felony charge after allegedly striking a U.S. Forest Service firefighter with his vehicle while attempting to bypass a road closure during an active forest fire Saturday evening.

Tommy Broadnax was charged with simple assault on a firefighter following the approximately 5:45 p.m. incident on Stephen Earl Drive in the Latimer Community, according to Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter.

Firefighters and U.S. Forest Service personnel had closed the roadway while working to contain a forest fire in the area. item.title: Yee-haw & you're welcome: We're celebrating Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STATEWIDE — Every year on March 27th, country music fans and lovers of linguistic absurdity unite to celebrate one of the most delightfully niche holidays on the calendar: Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day. It’s a day to tip your hat to the poets, the heartbroken, and the genuinely unhinged wordsmiths and writers who gave us some of the most wonderfully weird song titles in music history.

Your Hometown Country US 96.3’s Traci Lee immediately thought of the song “Ticks” by Brad Paisley, because the deeper meaning is… “I wanna check you for ticks.” US 96.3’s morning show host, Gordo, couldn’t immediately pick a favorite, but said he was sure it had something to do with tractors. Well guess what, Gordo, there’s a tractor in the top 5.

Country music has always had a special relationship with the ridiculous. While other genres sometimes aim for the profound or the cool, country music has never been afraid to get specific about being silly. Where else could a man earnestly record a song called “I’ve Been Flushed from the Bathroom of Your Heart” (and have it be Johnny Cash, no less) and have audiences sing along like, “Yeah, I’ve been there?”

The tradition runs deep. From Loretta Lynn and Conway Twitty harmonizing on “You’re the Reason Our Kids Are Ugly” to Bobby Bare asking the Lord to “Drop Kick Me Jesus Through the Goalposts of Life,” country music has long understood that life is funny, really messy, and worth writing songs about, no matter how absurd it sounds when you call the request line.

It seems like there’s actually a philosophy buried in the silliness. Country music titles tend to be hyper-specific: It’s a particular store, a particular animal, a particular piece of farm equipment. That specificity is what makes them so funny. “She Got the Gold Mine (I Got the Shaft)” by Jerry Reed isn’t just a joke. It’s a whole divorce settlement process summarized in a jaunty little country tune.

Here’s our Top 15:

“You’re the Reason Our Kids Are Ugly” — Conway Twitty & Loretta Lynn “She Got the Gold Mine (I Got the Shaft)” — Jerry Reed “I’ve Been Flushed from the Bathroom of Your Heart” — Johnny Cash “Dirty Old Egg-Sucking Dog” — Johnny Cash “She Thinks My Tractor’s Sexy” — Kenny Chesney “Get Your Tongue Outta My Mouth ‘Cause I’m Kissing You Goodbye” — Carlene Carter “I Still Miss You Baby, But My Aim’s Gettin’ Better” — various artists “If My Nose Was Running Money, I’d Blow It All on You” — Aaron Wilburn “Drop Kick Me Jesus Through the Goalposts of Life” — Bobby Bare “Tequila Makes Her Clothes Fall Off” — Joe Nichols “I’m Gonna Miss Her (The Fishin’ Song)” — Brad Paisley “It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels” — Kitty Wells “One Piece at a Time” — Johnny Cash (about stealing a Cadillac part by part) “Redneck Yacht Club” — Craig Morgan “If You Can’t Bite, Don’t Growl” — various artists

So on March 27 of each year, while you’re two-stepping in your kitchen to the newest hits on Your Hometown Country US96.3, crying into your sweet tea over some 1994 ballad on 93.5 The Legend, or just sitting on the porch wondering why your dog looks at you like that, take a moment to appreciate the unsung heroes of country music: the title writers. The ones who looked at a blank page, thought about heartbreak, truck payments, and bad luck, and decided the only reasonable response was to take the humanity of it to the most ridiculous place possible.

Happy Quirky Country Music Song Titles Day, from Darkhorse Press. Now go call your mama. You know she worries.

item.title: STEPPING UP TO SERVE: Hal’s St. Paddy’s krewes bring joy to Children’s of Mississippi patients - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Patients at Children’s of Mississippi got a special dose of joy this week when krewes from Hal’s St. Paddy’s Parade & Festival brought a parade-sized celebration right to them, complete with mini floats and festive throws.

The visit tied one of Jackson’s most loved spring traditions directly to the children and families it helps support. Hal’s St. Paddy’s Parade, often described by organizers as a “green Mardi Gras,” is a longtime downtown Jackson celebration known for its colorful floats and community spirit. Organizers say the festival honors the legacy of Hal White, celebrates downtown Jackson and supports Children’s of Mississippi.

This year’s main parade is set for noon Saturday, March 28, in downtown Jackson. Festival events also include pet and children’s parades at Smith Park, part of a larger weekend celebration that has become a signature event for the capital city.

For the young patients who got an early visit, the parade came in a smaller form, but certainly made their days.

item.title: Pedestrian Struck by Vehicle Near JSU; Capitol Police Investigating - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A pedestrian was injured after being struck by a vehicle Friday night near the intersection of Evergreen Avenue and University Boulevard, according to the Mississippi Capitol Police.

Officers responded to the scene around 8:46 p.m. March 26 and found an individual in the roadway who had been hit by a vehicle. The victim was transported to a nearby hospital. Authorities did not immediately release the person’s condition or identity.

The circumstances surrounding the crash remain unclear, and investigators have not said whether the driver remained at the scene.

Capitol Police said the case is an open and ongoing investigation and declined further comment.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Capitol Police at 601-540-0546.

item.title: Newton man charged with 2 counts of aggravated assault after shooting investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
NEWTON – A Newton man has been charged with two counts of aggravated assault following a shooting investigation early Wednesday morning, according to the Newton Police Department.

Police said officers were called to the area of Bingham Street around 6:15 a.m. March 25 after receiving reports of shots fired.

After investigating, authorities charged Jakolby Kamarion Billups of Newton with two counts of aggravated assault.

Police said Billups had been out on a felony bond at the time of his arrest. He is being held at the Newton County Jail pending his initial appearance.

The case will be forwarded to the District Attorney’s Office for prosecution.

Police Chief McKenzie Patrick thanked officers for their work on the case and also thanked the community for helping investigators resolve the case quickly.
